scope: Finite protocol obligations tied to exact source/test references and optional matching assurance execution evidence; not an exhaustive whole-implementation proof.

contracts.claim: SOCKS5 accepts only no-auth CONNECT with valid version/reserved/address/UTF-8/nonzero-port fields; IPv4, IPv6 and DOMAIN parsing consumes exactly the request and retains following application bytes.
contracts.bounds: Generated addresses up to 255 bytes, each request prefix EOF, short reads/writes, every byte of the fixed discriminants.

contracts.claim: Initial payload capture respects the protocol cap and 4096-byte implementation cap and yields empty input when its 2ms deadline expires.
contracts.bounds: Existing finite waiting-input/cap/deadline fixtures; not a proof of scheduler timing.

contracts.claim: A real camouflage TLS client rejects an untrusted origin chain or mismatched SNI, then succeeds after corrected trust or SNI. Its Certificate parsers require exact outer/list consumption; the compressed parser also requires a complete, exactly consumed zlib stream before certificate verification. Server Certificate contexts are empty and chains/entries nonempty; ALPN and CertificateVerify consume their complete vectors before state commits. Chain validation occurs at Certificate before parsing CertificateVerify/Finished or waiting for another record.
contracts.bounds: Fresh generated CA/leaf, a wrong CA or DNS name, explicit client rejection and no target connection. Parser fixtures include valid positive controls, each one-to-four-byte checksum truncation, zlib/outer-vector trailing bytes and bytes after Certificate.certificate_list in raw and compressed paths.
external_conditions: Binary trust-recovery fixtures require Unix child processes and loopback TCP/UDP sockets; temporary CA is trusted only by children. Parser fixtures use synthetic certificate bytes and do not independently prove certificate-chain validation.

contracts.claim: The real TLS validator requires the original 32-byte session ID echo, TLS 1.3 and valid extension framing; the extraction helper separately rejects truncated nested lengths. Both real readers reassemble fragmented ServerHello while retaining matching original record bytes for ParallaX key derivation; TLS hashes only the logical handshake. Existing TLS 1.2 coalesced-record forwarding/rejection behavior is preserved.
contracts.bounds: Finite strict-validator fixtures plus generated extraction fields and every truncated prefix. Reassembly is capped at 65,611 message bytes and 256 records; the server uses one total 8-second deadline. Tests cover every split of the fixture, a maximum extension vector, truncated/oversized/interleaved fragments and both legacy strict-mode outcomes.

contracts.claim: One supported TLS HelloRetryRequest rewrites only the requested key share/cookie, collapses the transcript and emits one compat CCS before ClientHello2.
contracts.bounds: Synthetic HRR groups/cookies and captured second-flight bytes.
external_conditions: The documented authenticated-proxy HRR transcript limitation remains; these are TLS retry checks, not successful proxy establishment through an HRR origin.

contracts.claim: Masked TCP authentication bytes bind SNI, random, public key, timestamp and nonce; wrong PSK/static pin falls through to the origin without opening a target.
contracts.bounds: Independent HMAC/HKDF carrier construction plus real child-binary rejection/recovery.
external_conditions: Unix child processes and loopback TCP/UDP sockets; temporary CA is trusted only by children.

contracts.claim: All-zero X25519 shared secrets are rejected before initial/auth/hybrid derivation succeeds.
contracts.bounds: Three production derivation entry points, explicit degenerate-secret fixtures.

contracts.claim: Freshness/skew, nonce/transcript replay, full capacity and persistent journal integrity are distinct decisions; cache pressure cannot evict a fresh replay guard.
contracts.bounds: Generated small cache histories plus actual server journal replay/capacity/corruption and source-admission fixtures.
external_conditions: Unix child processes and loopback TCP/UDP sockets; temporary CA is trusted only by children.

contracts.claim: The TLS-to-PQ handoff drains complete records and preserves buffered H2 bytes; a partial-record timeout/EOF does not establish a clean boundary.
contracts.bounds: Controlled fragmented records, paused/bounded deadlines and H2 phase boundaries.

contracts.claim: Finished is accepted only after the required encrypted-extensions/certificate-verification order and with correct verify_data.
contracts.bounds: Finite handshake-flight state and MAC fixtures; cryptographic hardness is assumed.

contracts.claim: Initial/hybrid/epoch/substream derived bytes match an independent HKDF/HMAC oracle; malformed ML-KEM keys/ciphertexts are rejected.
contracts.bounds: Specified key-schedule labels and bounded PSK/epoch/stream-ID vectors; not a proof of ML-KEM.

contracts.claim: ML-DSA identity signatures bind the transcript, PQ wire exchange and epoch; a wrong pinned identity closes before target dial.
contracts.bounds: Independent serialization and generated key/signature fixtures plus wrong-pin child process.
external_conditions: Unix child processes and loopback TCP/UDP sockets; temporary CA is trusted only by children.

contracts.claim: The actual client identity-flight reader requires bounded contiguous PX1I chunks and rejects EOF, malformed framing, wrong AEAD and prior-epoch records.
contracts.bounds: Actual async caller over bounded in-memory records, including the exact configured payload limit.

contracts.claim: CONNECT preserves host/port/initial payload and rejects zero/oversized fields, truncation and trailing bytes according to the independent wire parser.
contracts.bounds: Generated 1–255-byte hosts and bounded payloads plus the differential malformed corpus.

contracts.claim: PX1Q/PX1K/PX1S lengths, cipher-suite tags and fields match the independent wire oracle; invalid lengths/suite values fail.
contracts.bounds: Bounded valid records with every truncation and single-bit mutation of the differential seeds.

contracts.claim: Chunk declarations remain bounded and ordered; malformed/repeated offsets do not produce a false completion and a completed PX1F reassembler can be reused.
contracts.bounds: Generated payloads up to 4096 bytes, malformed sequence/resource corpus, PX1F/PX1I wire parser differential.

contracts.claim: All MUX kinds preserve fields and prefix consumption across concatenated frames; invalid kinds/framing fail independently of encoding success.
contracts.bounds: Five frame kinds, generated stream IDs/payloads, independent mutated/truncated corpus.

contracts.claim: UDP offer/request/decline/probe status and speed commands preserve their exact fields, lengths and canonical encoding; unknown extensible values retain their specified compatibility semantics.
contracts.bounds: All current control-command families; fixed probe statuses and generated version/reason/CC/FEC/byte-count fields.

contracts.claim: Both record ciphers and directions match independent ciphertext/plaintext oracles; tampering, reflected directions and replay do not yield plaintext.
contracts.bounds: AES-256-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305, bounded payload/padding, sequence carry and fresh-key rekey.

contracts.claim: Nonce reservations do not wrap; serial/parallel AEAD usage limits are enforced before output/callbacks and a fresh rekey resets the usage epoch.
contracts.bounds: Exact synthetic counter/budget boundary states; no millions-of-record timing experiment required.

contracts.claim: A failed parallel batch publishes no partial output, consumes its reserved nonce range and poisons future operations even across rekey.
contracts.bounds: Injected worker/open failures and finite mixed serial/parallel batches. Inline and background worker panic preserve the original panic payload, output prefix, consumed range and permanent poison.

contracts.claim: Padding trailers are bounded and removed exactly; record construction rejects unusable/over-cap lengths without leaking unfinished plaintext into committed output.
contracts.bounds: Finite exact-capacity, oversized trailer and unfinished builder fixtures.

contracts.claim: MUX stream ordering, half-close and peer reset semantics survive the actual relay path rather than only codec roundtrips.
contracts.bounds: Actual loopback carrier and stream control fixtures.
external_conditions: Unix loopback sockets; this is not all possible async schedules.

contracts.spec: ### 9.3 Mux scheduling and liveness (implementation behavior, wire-transparent)
contracts.claim: Concurrent streams preserve identity and a stalled stream does not block unrelated traffic; binary TCP and QUIC MUX paths must actually be selected.
contracts.bounds: Finite concurrent distinct payloads, stalled-stream fixture and explicit carrier-selection logs.
external_conditions: Unix child processes and loopback TCP/UDP sockets; temporary CA is trusted only by children.

contracts.claim: A client-selected private target is rejected after authentication with no target connection; operator-fixed loopback fixtures do not bypass this test.
contracts.bounds: One actual private target, explicit production denial/EOF, and a FIFO observer that requires a 250ms quiet window; a delayed real target-dial canary must fail the observation.
external_conditions: Unix child processes and loopback TCP/UDP sockets; temporary CA is trusted only by children.

contracts.claim: QUIC packet headers/numbers match independent layout/nearest-candidate oracles, preserve boundaries and reject reserved/unsupported forms.
contracts.bounds: Generated legal packet-number windows/CIDs and malformed/truncated header classes.

contracts.claim: QUIC Initial key material matches RFC 9001 and protected payload/header composition rejects tampering.
contracts.bounds: RFC vector plus every supported suite's finite seal/open/header-protection fixtures.

contracts.claim: Every implemented QUIC frame family preserves fields; truncation, unknown types and ACK underflow fail closed without resynchronization.
contracts.bounds: All implemented frame variants, bounded payloads and generated varint/length/range boundaries.

contracts.claim: Protected packet allocation never reuses a number or advances on rejection, and receive-range eviction cannot reopen a replay window.
contracts.bounds: Generated set-model histories and synthetic sequence/confidentiality limits.

contracts.claim: ACK/discard/loss histories conserve in-flight bytes, pure-ACK tracking stays bounded and RTT estimates match integer RFC EWMA equations.
contracts.bounds: Bounded generated packet/ACK/time histories; no live-network loss distribution claim.

contracts.claim: RESET_STREAM accounts for final size and releases connection credit; sequential streams replenish limits without retaining unbounded finished state.
contracts.bounds: Deterministic sans-I/O peer pairs and finite sequential/large-transfer fixtures.

contracts.claim: Pre-Finished ciphertext cannot commit key-phase state; premature/unacknowledged updates and exhaustion fail closed, and closed peers drain then become quiet.
contracts.bounds: Synthetic key generations/confidentiality budgets, deterministic timers and close ordering.

contracts.claim: H2 frame headers preserve all 24 length bits and reserved stream-ID semantics, and opening preface/settings/ACK behavior matches the wire shape.
contracts.bounds: Literal preface/setting encodings, bounded payloads, declared 24-bit length boundary classes and batched settings.

contracts.claim: H3 stream/frame varints accept legal non-minimal encodings, preserve prefix consumption and reject truncated/over-cap length claims.
contracts.bounds: All four varint widths, bounded payloads, 1MiB cap and hostile 32/62-bit declared lengths.

contracts.claim: H3 SETTINGS syntax and the subsequent exact Safari shape check are distinct: the actual shape rejects reordering, duplicates, extra entries and wrong fixed values.
contracts.bounds: Independent varint-pair oracle, generated GREASE derivation, every prefix and invalid three-setting shape class.

contracts.claim: Static QPACK literals and name references decode independent non-Huffman encodings; dynamic references, bad indices, invalid UTF-8/Huffman and oversize claims fail.
contracts.bounds: Bounded raw literal strings, integer continuation boundaries, specified static indices and malformed reference corpus.

contracts.claim: Exporter auth tokens bind both the PSK and live session/offer context; a token cannot transfer between sessions or offers.
contracts.bounds: Independent length-prefixed context hash and real loopback QUIC exporter pairs.
external_conditions: Loopback UDP sockets; standard cryptographic collision assumptions apply.

contracts.claim: A correct bidi probe verifies, wrong token/malformed reply is rejected, and server-declined UDP retains successful TCP operation with shared retry suppression.
contracts.bounds: Actual H3 request bidi and bounded probe outcomes; server decline observed through production child logs.
external_conditions: Unix child processes and loopback TCP/UDP sockets; temporary CA is trusted only by children.

contracts.claim: A second session actually accepts early data; ticket replay falls back to 1-RTT and single-use state persists over server restart.
contracts.bounds: Two controlled sessions, replay and disk-backed restart; actual server early-data acceptance assertions.
external_conditions: Loopback TCP/UDP sockets and temporary ticket/replay state.

contracts.claim: Unauthenticated TLS is relayed to the actual origin and the proxy remains usable; Safari GREASE/cipher opening constraints are checked separately.
contracts.bounds: Trusted local origin byte exchange and finite captured/template constraints.
external_conditions: Unix loopback fixtures. Statistical indistinguishability and live-censor resistance require separate field measurements.

contracts.claim: The actual QUIC TLS client and server reject incorrect or wrong-length Finished MACs without completing the handshake; fragmented valid Finished messages commit client application state or server ticket issuance only after complete verification.
contracts.bounds: Real peer-produced handshake flights with flipped, short, long and empty MACs plus bounded fragmentation. Client rejection preserves transcript/state and produces no application keys/exporter; server rejection prevents completion/tickets, while its earlier TLS-permitted application write keys remain installed.
external_conditions: Controlled certificate-verifier fixtures isolate Finished authentication; certificate-chain validation has separate evidence. Cryptographic hardness is assumed.

contracts.claim: Ticket expiry, suite/ALPN mismatch, invalid sealed tickets, missing early-data offer and incorrect binders reject PSK selection before consulting the single-use guard; guard refusal also prevents early-data acceptance, with real certificate-handshake fallback.
contracts.bounds: Seven server ticket/offer cases include a valid positive control and counted guard rejection. A separate client fixture removes only early_data from a real PSK offer, recomputes a correct binder and confirms the parsed PSK identity/binder remain present. Pre-guard rejection requires zero guard calls; valid and guard-refused offers call once. All rejected PSK offers complete an ordinary 1-RTT certificate handshake with matching exporters.
external_conditions: Synthetic sealed-ticket state and controlled certificate-verifier fixtures; durable replay/restart behavior remains a separate zero-rtt contract.

contracts.claim: The actual QUIC client Certificate state accepts only a complete, exactly consumed zlib CompressedCertificate with matching bounded output length, preserves the compressed wire transcript and rejects malformed inputs before advancing state. Invalid server context or empty chain is terminal, including when a later valid flight arrives in separate CRYPTO packets; the client endpoint sends CRYPTO_ERROR 0x132. TCP and QUIC distinguish malformed vectors (50), unoffered algorithms or declared resource-limit violations (47), and decompression/output-length failures (42).
contracts.bounds: Normal and exact 256KiB inflated certificate bodies; unsupported algorithm, declared/inflated over-cap output, mismatched length, invalid zlib, truncated vector/checksum and outer/stream trailing bytes. Rejection preserves the Certificate state, empty chain and pre-message transcript.
external_conditions: Controlled certificate-verifier fixture. Successful parser cases stop at CertificateVerify; they do not claim a complete authenticated handshake over the modified compressed transcript.

contracts.claim: The actual streaming H3 relay reader rejects non-DATA and over-cap frames and distinguishes partial-header/payload FIN from clean frame-boundary FIN, preserving preceding complete records.
contracts.bounds: In-memory byte cuts through two nonminimal eight-byte varints and a DATA body, malformed frame type/1MiB+1 length, plus actual QUIC FIN after a complete record and each malformed tail. Empty streams and complete zero-length DATA frames remain clean positive controls.
external_conditions: Loopback QUIC is required for the production H3DataFrameLegReader classification check. These are framing tests, not an independent AEAD oracle.

contracts.claim: Both relay roles require an authenticated exact TCP DONE marker after QUIC transfer; wrong marker/tag or missing TCP data fails, an in-flight valid DONE may finish during the post-QUIC-close grace, and an alive QUIC peer cannot suppress the absolute read backstop.
contracts.bounds: Both directions consume preceding relay-tail records before DONE to check nonce continuity. Wrong marker, bad AEAD, empty/partial-header TCP EOF, actual QUIC close followed by completion or expiry of the two-second grace, and the 120-second read backstop under paused time with continuously exchanged QUIC liveness bytes. The backstop cases do not simulate a blocked TCP write.
external_conditions: Serial ignored library tests require loopback TCP/UDP sockets; the absolute-backstop fixtures also require Tokio paused-clock controls.
